key_insight: WebSwarm turns web search into a recursive delegation process, letting agent nodes split, expand, and aggregate work to handle both deep reasoning and broad coverage at the same time.
engineering_relevance: The framework suggests a practical orchestration pattern for building more scalable research agents that can adapt search depth, collaboration, and evidence collection during inference.
method: Probes how information is organized on the web before expanding the search tree.
Dynamically instantiates agentic search nodes with local objectives and search modes.
Each node can solve locally or delegate child nodes, then return evidence upward for revision or aggregation.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports consistent improvements over single-agent and multi-agent baselines on BrowseComp-Plus, WideSearch, DeepWideSearch, and GISA, with additional ablations and efficiency analyses.
watch_item: Recursive delegation and dynamic node spawning may increase orchestration complexity and search cost if search-mode control or evidence grounding is not carefully managed.
paper_title: WebSwarm: Recursive Multi-Agent Orchestration for Deep-and-Wide Web Search
